name: General Public
description: General urban and rural residents carrying out daily commutes, shopping, and regular lifestyle tasks.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Life-threatening environmental heat load. Strict restriction of non-emergency movement.
precautions: Remain indoors in shaded, ventilated, or air-cooled environments between 11:00 AM and 4:30 PM.
Drink at least 3.5 to 4.5 litres of water with ORS, lemon water, or buttermilk throughout the day.
Check on vulnerable neighbours, children, and domestic pets.
symptoms_watch: Absence of sweating despite extreme heat

Very strong heat stress.summary: Dangerous heat conditions. Avoid prolonged direct sun exposure.
precautions: Avoid direct sun exposure between 12:00 PM and 3:30 PM.
Carry a wide-brim umbrella, sunglasses, and a reusable water bottle when traveling.
Wear loose-fitting, light-coloured breathable cotton clothing.
symptoms_watch: Muscle cramps in legs or abdomen

Strong heat stress.summary: Elevated thermal discomfort. Moderate hydration and sun protection required.
precautions: Drink water at regular 30-minute intervals before feeling thirsty.
Avoid heavy caffeine, alcohol, or carbonated sugary beverages.
Take regular rest in shaded or cooler areas.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Mild to moderate heat perception during midday hours.
precautions: Maintain steady baseline hydration.
Use sun protection (hats, umbrellas) during peak solar hours.

No thermal stress.summary: Comfortable thermal conditions. No heat-related physiological strain.
precautions: Enjoy outdoor activities normally.
Maintain standard dietary and hydration habits.
Light jacket or wrap for early mornings or hill tracts.

name: Outdoor Worker
description: Field technicians, delivery personnel, street vendors, and general outdoor service providers.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Mandatory stoppage of non-emergency outdoor physical labour. Extreme heatstroke risk.
precautions: Immediately halt heavy manual field tasks between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
Implement mandatory 20-minute shaded rest breaks every 40 minutes of work.
Provide chilled ORS electrolyte solutions at all work sites.
Mandatory buddy system to monitor coworkers for delirium or stumbling.

Very strong heat stress.summary: Heavy physiological strain. Shift strenuous shifts to early morning (6-10 AM) or late evening.
precautions: Reschedule heavy lifting or prolonged exposure away from 12:00 PM - 3:30 PM.
Mandatory 15-minute rest in shaded canopies every hour.
Consume 750ml of water/electrolytes per working hour.
Wear UV-reflective hats and wet neck towels.

Strong heat stress.summary: Increased sweat rate and metabolic fatigue. Structured rest cycles needed.
precautions: Enforce 10-minute shade breaks every 90 minutes.
Hydrate every 20 minutes regardless of thirst perception.
Ensure access to clean potable drinking water at workstations.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Manageable outdoor conditions with standard hydration practices.
precautions: Keep water bottles accessible on delivery vehicles or field kits.
Wear breathable protective gear.

No thermal stress.summary: Optimal conditions for outdoor work routines.
precautions: Standard work safety protocols.
Standard work attire.

name: Farmer
description: Agricultural cultivators, plantation workers, and irrigation labourers exposed to open sun and crop fields.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Critical open-field thermal hazard. Postpone field tilling and chemical spraying.
precautions: Complete agricultural tasks strictly before 10:30 AM or after 4:30 PM.
Avoid pesticide/fertilizer spraying during high heat (prevents respiratory stress).
Ensure livestock and draft animals have ample shaded shelters and clean water troughs.
Keep ORS packets and cool water jars under tree shades.

Very strong heat stress.summary: Severe open-field heat load. Shift heavy irrigation and harvest shifts.
precautions: Work in early morning shifts (5:30 AM to 10:30 AM).
Wear traditional cotton head wraps (thundu/gamcha) soaked in water.
Drink tender coconut water, buttermilk, and salted congee.
Take regular breaks under field trees.
Maintain hydration every 30 minutes.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Normal agricultural operations with routine hydration.
precautions: Carry adequate drinking water to the fields.

No thermal stress.summary: Favourable conditions for all farming activities.
precautions: Standard agricultural practices.
Light wrap for morning dews.

name: Ground/Construction Labourer
description: Workers engaged in masonry, steel bending, excavation, scaffolding, and road asphalt laying.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Dangerous site conditions due to direct radiation and thermal re-radiation from concrete and asphalt.
precautions: Enforce total stoppage of roofing, scaffolding, and asphalt pouring between 11 AM - 4 PM.
Employers must provide covered rest sheds with water-cooling fans/mist.
Provide chilled salted water / ORS free at every 50 metres on site.
Designate a trained site first-aid heat warden.

Very strong heat stress.summary: High risk of thermal exhaustion from heavy physical exertion.
precautions: Rotate workers every 45 minutes between high-exposure and shaded tasks.
Install temporary shade nets over outdoor mortar and cutting areas.
Mandatory 10-minute hydration pause every 45 minutes.

Strong heat stress.summary: Elevated metabolic load on building sites.
precautions: Provide continuous water refill stations.
Encourage wearing wide brim safety hard-hat shades.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Standard construction protocols with regular hydration checks.
precautions: Keep water coolers filled.
Standard occupational safety.
Standard PPE.

name: Corporation Worker
description: Municipal sanitary workers, street sweepers, waste collectors, drainage maintenance staff, and traffic wardens.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Urgent occupational thermal hazard for civic frontliners.
precautions: Reschedule sweeping and door-to-door waste collection strictly to 5:30 AM - 9:30 AM.
Supply electrolyte sachets and insulated thermal water bottles at ward offices.
Civic supervisors must conduct hourly wellness checks.
Provide resting access at government clinics and urban health centres.

Very strong heat stress.summary: High heat stress during sanitation routes.
precautions: Limit afternoon street sweeping.
Ensure light cotton reflective vests over synthetic uniforms.
Take 15-minute breaks in shaded municipal parks or bus shelters.

Strong heat stress.summary: Increased hydration requirements on daily routes.
precautions: Carry at least 2 litres of water with lemon/salt on sanitation carts.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Standard civic duties with hydration vigilance.
precautions: Drink water regularly.
Standard duties.
Light warm jacket.

name: IT Worker
description: Tech park and office professionals commuting across urban heat islands and transitioning between AC and hot outdoors.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Severe thermal shock risk during transit between air-conditioned buildings and scorching outdoor streets.
precautions: Advise remote work / work-from-home where possible to avoid peak traffic commutes.
Avoid walking outdoors during lunchtime (12:00 PM - 3:30 PM).
Allow 5 minutes of acclimatization in shaded foyers before stepping from cold AC into extreme outdoor heat.
Maintain hydration; dry AC environments mask respiratory fluid loss.

Very strong heat stress.summary: Avoid lunchtime outdoor walks in open urban concrete spaces.
precautions: Use indoor cafeterias or delivery.
Drink at least 2.5 litres of fluids even if working in cold rooms.
Keep cars shaded to prevent toxic volatile organic compound buildup inside hot vehicle cabins.
Carry water bottle for evening drive/train commute.
Maintain routine desk hydration.
Standard work day.
None.

name: School Student
description: Primary and secondary school children with immature thermoregulation and high physical play activity.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Critical child safety hazard. Schools should declare half-day or shift to morning sessions.
precautions: Mandatory ban on outdoor sports, assemblies, and physical training between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
Keep children in well-ventilated classrooms with active ceiling fans.
Introduce hourly 'Water Bell' periods where all students pause and drink water.
Parents and school vans must ensure ventilated transport with curtains/shades.

Very strong heat stress.summary: High heat stress for children. Cancel open-ground physical education.
precautions: Move physical education classes indoors or to shaded auditoriums.
Ensure water coolers on campus are filled with clean filtered water.
Ensure children wear lightweight loose school uniforms without blazers or ties.
Encourage students to drink a full bottle of water during school hours.
Limit playtime to shaded tree areas.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Normal school routines with hydration reminders.
precautions: Ensure children carry water bottles.

No thermal stress.summary: Perfect weather for outdoor sports and campus activities.
precautions: Standard school routines.
Light sweater for morning bus stops.

name: College Student
description: Young adults commuting across sprawling campuses, riding two-wheelers, and engaging in sports.

Extreme heat stress.summary: Severe campus thermal strain. High risk of dehydration during two-wheeler rides.
precautions: Reschedule inter-department sports and cultural outdoors to post-5:00 PM.
Wear UV-rated helmets with ventilated visors when riding bikes.
Hydrate with electrolyte juices between lecture halls.
Hostels should ensure open ventilation and access to cold water dispensers.
Avoid direct midday sun on campus grounds.
Carry water and wear sunglasses/hats during commutes.
Drink fluids regularly throughout the day.
Stay hydrated.

No thermal stress.summary: Ideal conditions for academic and sports events.
precautions: Enjoy campus life.
Light jacket.

name: Senior Citizen
description: Elderly individuals (60+ years) with reduced thirst sensation, cardiovascular vulnerability, and chronic medications.

Extreme heat stress.summary: CRITICAL LIFE SAFETY EMERGENCY. Very high mortality vulnerability from cardiovascular collapse and heat hyperpyrexia.
precautions: STRICTLY stay indoors in the coolest room of the house. Do NOT venture out.
Use wet sponge baths or cool foot soaks to assist physiological body cooling.
Drink water or electrolytes regularly even in the absence of thirst sensation.
Consult physician regarding dosage of diuretics or blood pressure medicines during heatwaves.
Family members must check on senior citizens at least three times daily.
symptoms_watch: Chest pain, fluttering pulse, or shortness of breath
Extreme weakness or inability to stand

Very strong heat stress.summary: Dangerous cardiovascular load on seniors. Restrict all outdoor walks.
precautions: Shift morning walks to before 6:30 AM; cancel evening walks if ambient air is above 35°C.
Keep curtains drawn and use room fans or evaporative coolers.
Sip small amounts of water, barley water, or tender coconut water every 30 minutes.

Strong heat stress.summary: Significant thermal strain for elderly individuals.
precautions: Avoid direct sun exposure.
Ensure comfortable light cotton loose clothing.
Keep hydration levels monitored.

Moderate heat stress.summary: Mild heat conditions. Senior citizens should remain conscious of fluid intake.
precautions: Drink fluids regularly throughout the day.

No thermal stress.summary: Pleasant, safe, and comfortable conditions for elderly wellness walks.
precautions: Normal healthy lifestyle routine.
Warm clothing for early morning walks to protect joint comfort.
